references.text: Parallel text about the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) on the tenth day of the seventh month, with a command to fast ('afflict your souls') and refrain from work
Repeats the command for the tenth day of the seventh month, to afflict souls and do no work
The expression 'everlasting statute' (חֻקַּת עוֹלָם) is also used here regarding Passover as a lasting ordinance
The same distinction between 'the native-born' (הָאֶזְרָח) and 'the foreigner' (הַגֵּר) living among the people, both subject to the same law
One law shall apply to both the native-born and the foreigner living among you
Further explanation in the same chapter about Sabbath rest and afflicting souls as an everlasting statute
The tenth day of the seventh month is also mentioned in connection with the Jubilee year and the Day of Atonement
Prophetic text about fasting and 'afflicting your soul' (תְּעַנּוּ נַפְשֵׁיכֶם), the same expression as in Leviticus
David describes how he afflicted his soul with fasting (בַּצּוֹם נַפְשִׁי)
Reference to 'the fast' (τὴν νηστείαν) in the NT, referring to Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement
NT text mentioning the high priest entering the Most Holy Place once a year, a reference to the Day of Atonement described in Leviticus 16
